source.title: A Method for Enhancing Generalization of Adam by Multiple Integrations
source.authors: Long Jin; Han Nong; Liang-Ming Chen; Zhenming Su

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the paper and appendix. Some layout is flattened, but the reported tables and prose are mostly recoverable.
record.tranche_reason: Compares an Adam modification with Adam and other optimizers on test accuracy and curvature, using a different intervention from the claim versions. It does not test the specific settings or measurements those versions name.
record.gate_note: The paper reports image, text, and label-noise experiments comparing MIAdam with Adam and other optimizers, plus Hessian-curvature comparisons. Cited results about other optimizers and flatness are not rows. Grid-search values used to select MIAdam hyperparameters are not rows.
record.test_reason: The study uses the flat-minima/generalization relationship to motivate MIAdam and evaluates its performance against Adam and variants. It does not compare adaptive methods with an SGD baseline for V4, or measure magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and generalization-gap rankings for V7. Its other experiments do not test V1–V8.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately paraphrases the authors' conclusion: MIAdam is claimed to improve generalization and label-noise robustness by finding flatter minima while preserving Adam-like overall convergence. Qualify the convergence statement: the multiple-integral phase alone can converge slowly or fail to converge, and the method switches to Adam; the appendix reports similar overall epochs to a steady state.
record.recipe_differences: Adds a multiple-integral term to Adam, uses it early in training, then switches to Adam; compares the resulting optimizer with Adam and variants. It does not reproduce an original claim-version method.
record.method_sensitivity: MIAdam order and switching moment vary across optimizer variants; label-noise rates vary from 20% to 80%; datasets and architectures vary. The paper reports MIAdam3 oscillating more than MIAdam2 in simulations and reports slower convergence or non-convergence before switching.

fits_no_version.finding: MIAdam1 has higher reported test accuracy than Adam in all retained image and text comparisons. Gains range from 0.03 percentage points for BERT/R8 to 5.86 points for AlexNet/ImageNet; these differences are not all established as statistically significant.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: An early multiple-integral phase followed by Adam can improve held-out classification accuracy relative to Adam under the tested recipes.

fits_no_version.finding: MIAdam1 exceeds Adam by 2.08, 2.77, 2.41, and 1.29 percentage points at 20%, 40%, 60%, and 80% label noise, respectively. Each condition has one run; MIAdam2 and MIAdam3 do not exceed Adam at every noise level.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: MIAdam1 improves clean-test accuracy relative to Adam when ResNet18 is trained on partially corrupted CIFAR-10 labels under this recipe.

fits_no_version.finding: Figure 3 reports lower top Hessian eigenvalues and traces for MIAdam variants than Adam. This is ordinary Hessian curvature, with an unresolved caption/prose disagreement about the architecture and dataset.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The tested multiple-integral Adam variants can reach solutions with lower unscaled Hessian curvature than Adam.

record.problems: The label-noise experiment has one run per optimizer and noise level. Main image and text tables report means and standard deviations over three runs. The text refers detailed experimental settings to the appendix. The supplied Figure 3 caption and nearby text describe DenseNet121 on CIFAR-100, while the extracted plot labels are not sufficient to securely identify every plotted value; figure-only curvature rows are therefore uncertain.
record.rows_left_out: Other optimizer-variant cells in Tables 1–3 and Table 4 were omitted to keep the record focused on Adam and MIAdam1 comparisons. The study does not test a listed claim version; the table and figure results are represented as findings under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Near-perfect fitting of fixed random labels paired with natural-label generalization and chance-level random-label held-out performance under the same recipe.
Test-error changes as width increases beyond the width required for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the contribution of local connectivity or initialization.

Adaptive versus SGD or momentum-SGD held-out performance under limited or broader tuning, including recovery of that difference through decoupled weight decay or switching. AdamW and SWATS are evaluated, but no SGD baseline establishes the claimed difference or its recovery.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that remove a large-batch penalty.
Dropout interventions, underfitting at excessive dropout, small-data effects, and joint removal of dropout and weight decay with augmentation.
Magnitude-aware perturbation tolerance versus training–test gaps at similarly low training loss, and rankings against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing examples selected by memorization influence and comparing retraining with equal-sized random removals.

record.verdict_notes: The retained accuracy rows are method-evaluation results, not evidence for a listed version. Their cannot_determine states concern applicability to V1–V8, not readability of their accuracy values. Figure 5 additionally attributes MIAdam's CIFAR-100/DenseNet121 improvement to generalization rather than training accuracy, but this still lacks the SGD comparison required for V4 and the sharpness measure required for V7. MIAdam receives grid search over its extra parameters; the reported performance should be understood within that tuning procedure.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label generalization coexistence.
Width sweeps beyond interpolation on one-hidden-layer ReLU networks.
Convolutional versus fully connected architectures and local connectivity.
Adaptive optimizers compared with SGD or momentum SGD under limited and broader tuning; the paper does not test those comparisons.
Large versus small batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout interventions and interactions with data augmentation or weight decay.
Magnitude-aware weight perturbation sharpness and its ranking against norm- and margin-based measures.
